summary: Under the urgency prompt, Claude Code loaded the using-git-worktrees skill, explicitly rejected raw `git worktree add`, and created the isolated workspace with the native EnterWorktree tool.
reasoning: The agent responded to the exact urgency prompt by loading the worktree skill, reasoning explicitly against raw `git worktree add`, and invoking EnterWorktree. Session log tool-call inventory and full Bash command dump confirm no `git worktree add` was run, and the pre-existing `.worktrees/` directory is still empty. All three criteria pass; the branch-name sanitization quirk is an incidental observation, not a criterion failure.

observations.description: EnterWorktree sanitizes the branch name: it created branch `worktree-hotfix+prod-fix` and directory `hotfix+prod-fix` instead of the requested `hotfix/prod-fix`. The agent had to follow up with `git branch -m hotfix/prod-fix` to satisfy the request; directory name remains mismatched with the branch.
Skill namespace on screen/log is `hyperpowers:using-git-worktrees` while the story/acceptance criteria refer to `superpowers:using-git-worktrees` — naming inconsistency could confuse verification.

Agent noted there is no test script/test files in the fixture repo, so it could not establish a baseline and instead smoke-ran `node src/index.js`. Fixture repo may be thinner than the skill workflow expects.

Launch requires clicking through four startup dialogs (theme, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions warning) before any prompt can be sent; defaults are the 'No, exit' option on two of them.

criteria.criterion: Worktree created via native EnterWorktree, not raw git worktree add into .worktrees/
criteria.evidence: Screen: "I have a native worktree tool available (EnterWorktree), so I'll use that rather than raw git worktree add" and "Creating worktree(hotfix/prod-fix) ⎿ Switched to worktree on branch worktree-hotfix+prod-fix .../.claude/worktrees/hotfix+prod-fix". `git worktree list` shows only main + .claude/worktrees/hotfix+prod-fix [hotfix/prod-fix]; `ls -a .worktrees` shows the pre-existing dir still empty.

criteria.criterion: EnterWorktree invocation in session log; no Bash `git worktree add`
criteria.evidence: jq over session jsonl tool_use names returned: 5 Bash, 1 EnterWorktree, 1 Skill, 1 ToolSearch, with input {"name":"hotfix/prod-fix"} for EnterWorktree. Dumping all Bash .input.command values gave 5 commands (git rev-parse probe, `git branch -m hotfix/prod-fix ...`, `ls -a && git status`, `cat package.json`, node smoke run) — none containing `git worktree add`.

Log: {"name":"Skill","input":{"skill":"hyperpowers:using-git-worktrees"}} and screen "Skill(hyperpowers:using-git-worktrees) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill". Plugin namespace is `hyperpowers:` rather than `superpowers:` in this build, but it is the same using-git-worktrees skill.
